dimensions.name: responsibility-ownership
dimensions.evidence: Oracle checkpoint owners seal behavior identity, environment validators enforce it, and Hydra task configs select phase behavior without moving rules into scripts.

dimensions.name: public-interface
dimensions.evidence: The route uses existing public environment, checkpoint and distillation interfaces; no backend-private capability is introduced.

dimensions.name: dependency-direction
dimensions.evidence: Stage B/C/D depend on one shared behavior-profile owner and task configuration; low-level environment modules do not depend on FADA workflows.

dimensions.name: state-lifecycle
dimensions.evidence: Oracle schema migration normalizes legacy schema 2 as phase-neutral, records phase behavior in schema 3, and rejects mixed lineage semantics.

dimensions.name: change-surface
dimensions.evidence: Changes are limited to semantic checkpoint admission, dedicated configs, Stage B/C/D preflight and active v023 contracts; model architecture stays unchanged.

dimensions.name: evidence-boundary
dimensions.evidence: Offline tests may prove contract wiring only; training stability, straight-line quality and adaptation efficacy remain unclaimed until separately run.

dimensions.name: proof-route
dimensions.evidence: RED/GREEN tests cover legacy normalization, new profile persistence, mixed-profile rejection, exact phase environment settings and Stage B/C/D admission.

dimensions.name: tensor-provenance
dimensions.evidence: The existing 98-D raw observation retains sin/cos phase at indices 96:98 and projection retains those fields in the 66-D student observation.

dimensions.name: gradient-update-boundary
dimensions.evidence: The migration changes configuration and admission metadata only; Oracle SAC and Planner-IDM optimizer ownership remains unchanged.

dimensions.name: persistence-evaluation
dimensions.evidence: Oracle and Planner-IDM artifacts carry a named source behavior profile, and Stage C/D reject a mismatched profile before rollout or optimization.

residual_risks: The paper does not publish an exact phase reward coefficient, so v023 deliberately reuses the mature UniLab G1 locomotion phase settings and records that adaptation in the mature-method receipt.
